name: Quilted cotton armour
description: A sleeveless jacket of raw cotton packed thick between two quilted layers and stiffened with salt, its neck and armholes bound in leather. Very heavy and very hot.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, collar towards +z, 480 mm across, 600 mm long and 40 mm thick: a sleeveless vest with a diamond lattice of khaki quilting over the cream cotton, deep armholes, a neck notch showing the khaki inside, and leather binding round the neck, down both armholes and along the hem. The padding is laid out flat rather than folded. Slot `torso`, as the gambesons have it: it is meant to be worn as the outer layer by itself. Protection is a judgement for very thick salted padding: strong against blows and cuts, fair against points. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Mild steel light chestplate
description: A thin mild steel breastplate and backplate strapped together, with a single lame at the hips and small guards for the shoulders.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, neck towards -z, about 600 mm from the shoulder straps to the fauld and 600 mm across the shoulder guards: a thin breastplate with one fauld lame below it and a single arched lame against each shoulder, a middle ridge and rolled neck and arm edges, the backplate's edge showing round the sides, tan leather shoulder straps buckled on the chest and side straps hanging loose. The breastplate lies over its backplate with the guards spread beside it. Plate in `steel-bright`, the finish for mild steel. Slot `vest`, as the cuirasses and plate suits of earlier armour batches have it, so a padded or cloth `torso` layer goes under it. The shoulder guards and fauld also reach the arms and upper legs; Deadvox gives a wearable one slot. Protection is a judgement for mild steel plate. The xl size shares the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Bronze bell cuirass
description: An old-style bronze breastplate and backplate, the chest and belly hammered in raised lines and the hem flared out like a bell.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, neck towards -z, 500 mm from the neck to the flared hem and 440 mm across it: a polished bronze breastplate over its duller backplate, raised lines under the chest and down the belly, a rolled rim round the neck and armholes, a flared band at the hem, two pins down each side and tan leather ties over the shoulders. The backplate fills the breast's curve, so the pair lies as one closed body. Slot `vest`, as the cuirasses and plate suits of earlier armour batches have it, so a padded or cloth `torso` layer goes under it. Protection is a judgement for hammered bronze plate. The xl and xs sizes share the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Leather lamellar cuirass
description: Rows of small hardened leather plates laced together into a cuirass, with short laced runs over the shoulders.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, neck towards -z, 560 mm from neck to hem and 740 mm across its shoulder guards: nine overlapping rows of chestnut leather plates laced across in tan, the neck open between two shoulder runs and bound in oxblood, the hem bound too, and a shorter laced panel either side for the shoulders. Laid out flat rather than packed. Slot `vest`, as the cuirasses and plate suits of earlier armour batches have it, so a padded or cloth `torso` layer goes under it. The shoulder panels also reach the arms. Protection is a judgement for laced hardened leather. The xl and xs sizes share the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
